spans.s:
कक् कक्, cl. 1. A. ककते, चकके, ककि-
तुम्, to be unsteady; to be proud; to be
thirsty; [cf. Lat. vacillo for qvacillo.]
कक्क् कक्क्, a various reading for कख्, q. v.

ककजाकृत ककजा-कृत, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved.
mutilated, torn to pieces.
ककन्द ककन्द, अस्, m. gold; N. of a king.
ककर ककर, अस्, m., Ved. a kind of bird.
काकार काकार, अस्, ई, अम्, scattering water.

ककर्दु ककर्दु, उस्, m. (?), Ved. destruction
of enemies.

ककाटिका ककाटिका, f., Ved. a part of the
back of the human head, (enumerated together with
मस्तिष्क, ललाट, and कपाल.)

ककुञ्जल ककुञ्जल, अस्, m. the bird Cātaka;
[cf. कपिञ्जल.]

ककुत्सल ककुत्सल, अस्, m., Ved. an ex-
pression of endearment applied to a child (?).

ककुद् ककुद्, त्, f. a peak or summit (cul-
men); chief, head; any projecting corner; the hump
on the shoulders of the Indian bull; a horn; an en-
sign or symbol of royalty, as, the white parasol &c.;
N. of a daughter of Dakṣa and wife of Dharma.
(According to native grammarians ककुद् is the form
which must be substituted for ककुद at the end of
compounds, e. g. त्रि-ककुद्, three-peaked.)
—ककुत्-
स्थ, अस्, m., N. of a grandson of Ikṣvāku and son
of Śaśāda, said to be so called because in a battle he
stood on the hump of Indra, who had been changed
into a bull; according to the Rāmāyaṇa he is a son
of Bhagīratha.
—ककुद्-मत् or ककुन्-मत्, आन्,
अती, अत्, running high (as a wave); furnished with a
hump; (आन्), m. a mountain; a buffalo with a hump
on his shoulders; N. of a medicinal plant; (ती), f. the
hip and loins; N. of a metre; [cf. Lat. cacûmen
and culmen for caculmen.]
—ककुद्मि-कन्या, f.
a river (‘mountain-daughter’).
—ककुद्-मिन्, ई, इनी,
इ, peaked, humped; (मी), m. a mountain; a buffalo
with a hump on his shoulders; an epithet of Viṣṇu;
[]
N. of a prince of the Ānartas; (इनी), f., N. of a river.
—ककुद्रुम, अस्, m. (for ककुद्-द्रुम ?), N.
of a jackal in the Pañcatantra.
—ककुद्-वत्, आन्, m.
a buffalo with a hump on his shoulders; (ती), f., N.
of the wife of Pradyumna.

काकुद् काकुद्, त्, f., Ved. and काकुद, अम्,
n. the hollow of the mouth, the palate.

ककुद, अस्, अम्, m. n. the summit of a moun-
tain; chief, pre-eminent; the hump on the shoulders
of the Indian bull; a species of serpent; an ensign
or symbol of royalty, as the white parasol, &c.
—ककुद-कात्यायन, अस्, m., N. of a Brāhman
who was a violent adversary of Śākya-muni.
—क-
कुदाक्ष (˚द-अक्˚), अस्, m., N. of a man.

ककुन्दर ककुन्दर, अम्, n. the cavities of
the loins; (ककुद्मती-दर?; cf. ककुद्मती and
कुकुन्दर.)

ककुभ् ककुभ्, प्, f. (connected with ककुद्),
a peak or summit (cacumen); space, region or quarter,
as east, west, &c.; N. of a metre of three Pādas con-
sisting of eight, twelve, and eight syllables respectively,
so called because the second Pāda exceeds the others
by four syllables; unornamented hair or the hair
hanging down as a tail; a wreath of Campaka
flowers; splendor, beauty; a Śāstra or sacred treatise;
a Rāgiṇī or personified mode of music; the personi-
fied quarter of the sky; a daughter of Dakṣa and
wife of Dharma.
काकुभ्, a various reading for काकुद्.

ककुभ, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. excelling, distinguished;
(अस्), m. a kind of goblin or evil spirit; the tree
Terminalia Arjuna; a part of a lute called the belly,
a wooden vessel covered with leather placed under its
neck to render the sound deeper, or a crooked piece
of wood at the end of the lute; one of the Rāgas or
personified musical modes; N. of a man; N. of a
mountain; (आ), f. space, region, quarter; one of the
Rāgiṇīs or female personifications of music.
—ककु-
भादनी (˚भा-अद्˚), f. ‘food of the sky,’ a kind of
fragrance or perfume; [cf. नली. ]

काकुभ काकुभ, अस्, आ, अम्, consisting of
Kakubh verses; a patronymic from Kakubh.
—का-
कुभ-बार्हत, अस्, m. (scil. प्रगाथ) a Pragātha
beginning with a Kakubh and ending with a Bṛhatī.

ककुह, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. eminent, excelling others,
excellent; (अस्), m., Ved. a part of a carriage, perhaps
the seat.

ककेरुक ककेरुक, अस्, m. a worm in the
stomach.

कक्कट कक्कट, अस्, m., Ved. a species of
animal, perhaps a kind of bird.
कक्कुल कक्कुल, अस्, m., N. of a Bhikṣu.

कक्कोल कक्कोल, अस्, m., N. of a plant bear-
ing a berry, the inner part of which is a waxy and
aromatic substance; (अम्), n. or कक्कोलक, अम्, n.
a perfume prepared from the berries of this plant.

काकोल काकोल, अस्, m. a raven [cf. काक
and काकाल]; a boar; a snake; a potter; (अस्, अम्),
m. n. a poisonous substance of a black colour or the
colour of a raven, whence its name; possibly the
berry of the Cocculus Indicus; (अम्), n. a division
of the infernal regions or hell; (अस्, ई), m. f. a
vegetable substance used in medicine, described as
[]
sweet and cooling, allaying fever, removing phlegm,
&c.; it is said to be a root brought from Nepal or
Morung.

कक्क्वल्ल कक्क्वल्ल, अस्, m. a patronymic of
Guṇacandra.

कक्ख् कक्ख्, a various reading for कख्,
q. v.

कक्खट कक्खट, अस्, आ, अम्, hard, solid;
(ई), f. chalk.
—कक्खट-पत्त्रक, अस्, m. the
plant Corchorus Olitorius; (rope is made from its
fibre.)

कक्ष कक्ष, अस्, m. (said to be fr. rt. कष्),
a lurking or hiding-place; an inner recess, the interior
of a forest; a forest of dead trees, a dry wood (the
lair of wild beasts), grass, dry grass; a spreading
creeper, a climbing plant; the armpit (as the most
concealed part of the human body); the side or flank;
the orbit of a planet or the circle anciently termed a
deferent; sin; a buffalo; a gate; the Beleric Myroba-
lan or Terminalia Belerica; (आ), f. painful boils in the
armpit, side, shoulder, &c.; an elephant's rope, the
string round his neck, also his girth; a woman's
girdle or zone; a surrounding wall, a wall; a place
surrounded by walls; a court or court-yard; an en-
closure; a secluded portion of an edifice; a private
or inner chamber, the private apartment for women
&c., a room in general; a particular part of a carriage;
[]
resemblance, similarity; objection or reply in argu-
ment; emulation, rivalry, object of emulation; the
jeweller's weight, the Retti; (अस्, आ), m. f. the end of
the lower garment which, after the cloth is carried
round the body, is brought up behind and tucked
into the waistband; a border, lace; the scale or basin
of a balance; (अम्), n. a star, a constellation (perhaps
a wrong reading for ऋक्ष); (आस्), m. pl., N. of a
people.
—कक्ष-धर, अम्, n. the part of the
body where the upper arm is connected with the
shoulder, the shoulder-joint.
—कक्ष-प, अस्, m.
one of the nine treasures of Kuvera; [cf. कच्छप.]
—कक्ष-पुट, अस्, m. the armpit; title of a
work on magic.
—कक्ष-रुहा, f. a fragrant grass,
Cyperus.
—कक्ष-शाय, अस्, m. a dog; [cf.
कङ्कशाय.]
—कक्ष-सेन, अस्, m., N. of a Rā-
jarshi.
—कक्ष-स्थ, अस्, आ, अम्, situated on the
side, seated on the hip or flank.
—कक्षाध्याय
(˚ष-अध्˚), अस्, m., N. of a part of a commentary
by Bhūdhara on the Sūrya-siddhānta.
—कक्षान्-
तर (˚ष-अन्˚), अम्, n. the inner or private
apartment.
—कक्षा-पट, अस्, m. a cloth passed
between the legs to cover the privities.
—कक्षा-
पुटि, इस्, m., N. of a physician; (wrong reading for
काक्षपुटि ?).
—कक्षावेक्षक, अस्, m. (कक्षा
+ अवेक्षक fr. rt. ईक्ष् with अव), a guard of the
inner or queen's apartments; keeper of a royal
garden; a door-keeper; a poet; a debauchee; a
player, a painter; warmth of feeling, strength of
sentiment.
—कक्षी-कृत, अस्, आ, अम्, assented, pro-
mised, (touching the armpit with the hand was per-
haps a manner of affirming anything; cf. उरसि कृ
under उरस्.)
—कक्षोत्था (˚ष-उत्˚), f. a fragrant
grass, Cyperus.

काक्ष काक्ष (का-अक्˚), अस्, आ, अम्, frowning,
looking scornfully or in displeasure; (अस्), m. a glance,
a wink or leer; (अम्), n. a frown, a look of dis-
pleasure; [cf. कटाक्ष.]
कक्षक, अस्, m., N. of a Nāga.
कक्षतु, उस्, m., N. of a plant.

कक्षाय, nom. A. कक्षायते, -यितुम्, to wait
for any one in a hidden place, lie in ambush; to
intend anything wicked.

कक्षीवत्, आन्, m. (fr. कक्ष्या), N. of a renowned
Ṛṣi, sometimes called Pajriya; he is the author of
several hymns of the Ṛg-veda, and is described in
legends as a son of Uśij and Dīrgha-tamas; (अन्तस्),
m. pl. the family or the descendants of Kakṣīvat.
काक्षीवत् काक्षीवत्, आन्, m. = कक्षीवत्.

कक्षेयु, उस्, m., N. of a son of Raudrāśva and
Ghṛtācī.

कक्ष्य, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. consisting of shrubs or
dry grass; secret; (Sāy.) filling the girth, as a well-fed
horse; (आ), f. the girth of an elephant or horse, con-
sisting of rope or leather; a woman's girdle or zone;
metaphorically the fingers (encircling the Soma cup);
an upper garment, the border or lace of one; the
enclosure of an edifice, i. e. either the wall &c. so en-
closing it, or the court or chamber constituting the
enclosure, the inner apartment of a palace; similarity;
effort, exertion; a shrub yielding the black and red
berry that serves as a jeweller's weight, the Retti or
Gunja, Abrus Precatorius; (अम्), n. the cup or re-
ceptacle of a balance; a part of a carriage.
—कक्ष्य-
प्र, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. filling the girth (as a well-fed
horse).
—कक्ष्या-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, furnished with
a girth.
—कक्ष्यावेक्षक, अस्, m. = कक्षा-
वेक्षक, q. v.
—कक्ष्या-स्तोत्र, अम्, n., N. of a
hymn by Divākara-vatsa.

काक काक, अस्, m. (said to be fr. rt. कै, to
caw), a crow, (metaphorically an expression of contempt,
e. g. न त्वां काकम् मन्ये, I value thee less than a
crow); an impudent, insolent fellow; a lame man, a
cripple; washing the head, bathing by dipping the
head only into the water as crows do; a sectarial
mark (तिलक); a particular measure; the plant
Ardisia Humilis (see काक-जम्बु); N. of a Dvīpa
or division of the world; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a people;
(ई), f. a female crow, personified as a daughter of
Kaśyapa by Tāmrā, and mother of the crows; a kind
of medicinal plant (= काकोली); N. of one of the seven
mothers of Śiśu; (आ), f., N. of several plants, Leea
Hirta, also = काक-जङ्घा, काक-नासा; Solanum
Indicum, = काक-माची; Ficus Oppositifolia, = काको-
डुम्बर; another medicinal plant, = काकोली; an-
other plant, commonly रक्तिका; (अम्), n. a multitude
or assemblage of crows; a modus coeundi.
—काक-
कङ्गु, उस्, f. a kind of panic-grass, Panicum Milia-
ceum.
—काक-कला, f. the plant Leea Hirta; [cf.
काक-जङ्घा.]
—काक-कूर्म-मृगाखु (˚ग-
आखु), अवस्, m. pl. the crow, tortoise, deer, and
mouse.
—काक-कूर्मादि (˚म-आदि), अयस्, m. pl.
the crow, the tortoise, and the rest.
—काक-घ्नी, f.
a tree, said to be a large kind of Karañja, Galedupa
Arborea, = महा-करञ्ज.
—काक-चण्डीश्वर, अस्,
m., N. of a man.
—काक-चिञ्चा, f. the shrub which
yields the red and black berry used in India as a
jeweller's weight, Abrus Precatorius; also काक-चिञ्चि
and काक-चिञ्ची.
—काक-चिञ्चिक, N. of a kind of
soft substance; another reading of the word is काचि-
लिन्दि.
—काक-च्छद, अस्, m. a wagtail; side-locks
of hair.
—काक-च्छदि, इस्, m. or, according to an-
other reading, काक-च्छर्दि, इस्, m. a wagtail; a
crow's vomit.
—काक-जङ्घा, f. the plant Leea
Hirta; also Abrus Precatorius.
—काक-जम्बु, उस्,
f. the plant Ardisia Humilis, commonly Bhumijamb;
(ऊस्), f. another species of Jambu.
—काक-जात, अस्,
m. the Indian cuckoo.
—काक-ता, f. the state of a
crow.
—काक-तालीय, अस्, आ, अम्, unexpected, as in
the fable of the fruit of the palm falling unexpectedly
at the moment of the alighting of a crow and killing
it; accidental; (अम्), ind. unexpectedly, suddenly;
(अम्), n. the fable of the crow and the fruit of the
palm.
—काकतालीय-वत्, ind. suddenly, (said of any
unexpected casualty.)
—काक-तालुकिन्, ई, इनी, इ,
having the palate of a crow, contemptible, vile.
—काक-तिक्ता, f. the plant Abrus Precatorius.
—का-
क-तिन्दुक, अस्, m. a kind of ebony, Diospyros
Tomentosa.
—काक-तुण्ड, अस्, m. the dark species
of Agallochum; (ई), f., N. of a tree, in Hindī called
Kauāḍoḍi; a sort of brass.
—काक-तुण्डिका, f. the
plant Abrus Precatorius.
—काक-तुल्य, अस्, आ, अम्,
like a crow, crow-like, crafty.
—काक-दन्त, अस्, m.
the tooth of a crow, i. e. anything impossible or not
existing.
—काक-दन्तकि, a patronymic from Kāka-
dantaka; (अयस्), m. pl., N. of a warrior-tribe; का-
कदन्तकीय, अस्, m. a prince of the Kākadantakis.
—काक-ध्वज, अस्, m. submarine fire, a personage
in Hindū mythology; [cf. और्व.]
—काक-नामन्,
आ, m. the plant Agati Grandiflora.
—काक-नाशा, f.
the same plant.
—काक-नास, अस्, m., N. of a plant,
commonly called Vikaṇṭaka; (आ), f. the plant Leea
Hirta.
—काक-नासिका, f. the plant Leea Hirta; N.
of another plant, also called Rakta-trivṛt.
—काक-
निद्रा, f. ‘a crow's sleep,’ a light slumber, one which
is easily broken.
—काक-नीला, f. = काक-जम्बू.
—काक-पक्ष, अस्, m. side-locks of hair on the
temples of boys and young men; three or five locks
on each side left when the head is first shaved and
allowed to remain there, especially in persons of the
[]
military caste; (also at the end of compounds काक-
पक्षक.)
—काक-पद, अम्, n. the foot of a
crow; an incision in the skin similar to a crow's
foot; the sign V in MSS. marking that something
has been left out; (अस्), m. a modus coeundi.
—का-
क-पर्णी, f. the plant Phaseolus Trilobus.
—काक-
पीलु, उस्, m., N. of several plants, = काक-तिन्दुक,
काक-तुण्डी, and also a variety of Abrus Precatorius.
—काक-पीलुक, अस्, m. = काक-तिन्दुक.
—काक-
पुच्छ, अस्, m. the Kokila or Indian cuckoo, (perhaps
a Prākṛt form of the next.)
—काक-पुष्ट, अस्, m.
the Indian cuckoo, (this bird, like the English cuckoo,
being said to leave its eggs in the nests of other birds,
as in that of the crow &c.)
—काक-पुष्प, अम्, n.
= गन्ध-पर्ण (?).
—काक-पेय, अस्, आ, अम्,
what may be drunk by a crow, epithet of a shallow
river.
—काक-फल, अस्, m. the tree Azadirachta
Indica; (आ), f. = काक-जम्बू.
—काक-बन्ध्या, f.
a woman that bears only one child.
—काक-भाण्डी,
f. a species of Karañja.
—काक-भीरु, उस्, m. an
owl (‘afraid of crows’).
—काक-मद्गु, उस्, m. a
water-hen, a gallinule; resembling a crow in colour.
—काक-मर्द, अस्, m. a kind of gourd, Cucumis
Colocynthis (महा-काल).
—काक-मर्दक, अस्,
m. the same.
—काक-माचिका or काक-माची, f. the
plant Solanum Indicum, an esculent vegetable, com-
monly Gūrkamai.
—काक-माता, f. the same plant.
—काक-मुख, आस्, m. pl. ‘crow-faced,’ N. of a
mythical people.
—काक-मुद्गा, f. a plant, com-
monly Mugani; according to some a wild kind of
bean, Phaseolus Trilobus.
—काक-मृग, औ, m. du.
the crow and the deer.
—काक-यव, अस्, m. barren
corn, the ear of which has no grains.
—काक-रुद्र-
संवाद, अस्, m. title of a work on omens.
—काक-
रुहा, f. a parasite plant, Epidendrum Tesseloides &c.
—काक-वत्, ind. like a crow, in the manner of a
crow.
—काक-वर्ण, अस्, m., N. of a prince.
—का-
क-वर्णिन्, ई, m., N. of a prince.
—काक-वर्तक,
औ, m. du. the crow and the quail.
—काक-वल्लभा,
f. = काक-जम्बू.
—काक-वल्लरी, f., N. of a plant,
= स्वर्ण-वल्ली.
—काक-व्याघ्र-गोमायु, अवस्,
m. pl. the crow, the tiger, and the jackal.
—काक-
शब्द, अस्, m. the cawing of a crow.
—काक-शिम्बी,
f., N. of a plant, = काक-तुण्डी.
—काक-शीर्ष, अस्,
m. the tree Agati Grandiflora, commonly called Va-
kapuṣpa.
—काक-शीर्षि, इस्, m., N. of a man.
—काक-स्त्री, f. the same plant.
—काक-स्फूर्ज,
अस्, m. the plant Diospyros Tomentosa.
—काक-
स्वर, अस्, m. a shrill tone.
—काकाक्षि (˚क-अक्˚),
n. the eye of a crow; काकाक्षि-न्यायेन, ind. in
the manner of a crow's eye, (crows are supposed to
have but one eye or visual orb, which, as occasion
requires, moves from the cavity on one side into that
on the other); a term for a word which follows two
rules.
—काकाङ्गा or ई (˚क-अङ्˚), f. the plant Leea
Hirta, = काक-नासा.
—काकाञ्ची, f. the plant Leea
Hirta; an esculent vegetable, Solanum Indicum.
—का-
काण्ड (˚क-अण्˚), अस्, m., N. of two plants, Mahā-
nimba and Kākatindu (?), a kind of bean; (आ), f. a
kind of spider; N. of a plant; see कोलशिम्बी.
—काकाण्डक, अस्, m., N. of a crow or N. of a
plant; a kind of spider.
—काकाण्डोला, f., N. of a
plant.
—काकादनी (˚क-अद्˚), f., N. of several
plants, Abrus Precatorius; a white variety of this
plant, commonly Śveta-guñjā.
—काकारि (˚क-अरि),
इस्, m. an owl.
—काकेक्षु (˚क-इक्˚), उस्, m. a kind
of reed, Saccharum Spontaneum.
—काकेन्दु (˚क-

—काकेष्ट (˚क-इष्˚), अस्, m. the
tree Melia Azadirachta.
—काकोडुम्बर (˚क-उड्˚),
अस्, m. or काकोडुम्बरिका, f. or काकोदुम्बरिका,

—का-
कोदर (˚क-उद्˚), अस्, m. a serpent.
—काकोलूक

—काकोलूकिका, f.

—काकोलू-
कीय, अम्, n. = the preceding; N. of the third book

ठक (˚क-ओष्ठ), अस्, इका, अम्, shaped like the

काकण, अम्, n. a leprosy with black and red
spots, considered incurable; (called so from its
[]
similarity to the black and red seed of the plant
Abrus Precatorius.)
काकणन्तिका, f. the plant Abrus Precatorius.
काकणि, a sort of small coin; [cf. काकिणी.]
काकनन्ती, f. the plant Abrus Precatorius.
काकायु, उस्, m., N. of a plant, = काकवल्लरी.
काकाल, अस्, m. a raven; [cf. काक and काकोल.]

काकल काकल, अम्, n. a jewel worn upon
the neck.
काकीय, अस्, आ, अम्, relating to a crow.

काकतीयरुद्र काकतीय-रुद्र, अस्, m., N. of
a king of Nāgapura.

काकन्दि काकन्दि, अयस्, m. pl., N. of a
warrior-tribe.
काकन्दी, f., N. of a country; Emblic Myrobalan.
काकन्दीय, अस्, m. a prince of the above tribe.

काकम्बीर काकम्बीर, अस्, m., Ved., N. of a
tree; (according to Sāy. literally ‘a crow-bearer.’)

काकरुक काकरुक or काकरूक, अस्, आ, अम्,
timid, afraid, a coward; naked; poor, indigent;
(अस्), m. a hen-pecked husband; an owl; fraud,
deceit.

काकलक, अस् or अम्, m. or n. (?), the top of the
windpipe; the thyroid cartilage; (अस्), m. an orna-
ment of the neck; a species of rice.

काकलि काकलि, इस्, f. a soft sweet sound
[cf. कल]; N. of an Apsaras; (ई), f. a low and
sweet tone; a musical instrument with a low tone
played to ascertain whether a person is asleep or not.
—काकली-द्राक्षा, f. a kind of grape without a
stone or with a very small one.
—काकली-रव, अस्,
m. the Kokila or Indian cuckoo.
काकलीक, अस्, अम्, m. n. (?) a low sweet tone.

काकिणी काकिणी, f. a small coin, a small
sum of money equal to twenty Kapardas or cowries,
or to a quarter of a Paṇa; the seed of Abrus Preca-
torius used as a weight; the shell Cypræa Moneta or
cowrie used as a coin; a cubit, the fourth part of a
Daṇḍa or short pole; a Daṇḍa; a part of a measure.
काकिणिका, f. = the preceding; an atom, a particle.
काकिणीक, अस्, आ, अम्, having the value of a Kākiṇī.

काकिनी, f. the fourth part of a Paṇa; a quarter of
a Māna; the shell Cypræa Moneta.

काकिल काकिल, अस्, m. a jewel worn upon
the neck; [cf. काकल.]

काकु काकु, उस्, f. change of the voice in
fear, anger, grief, &c. [cf. सेवा-काकु]; muttering,
murmuring; the tongue; stress, emphasis.

काकुत्स्थ काकुत्स्थ, अस्, m. a descendant of
Kakutstha; an epithet of Anenas, Aja, Daśaratha,
Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa; N. of a sovereign, also Purañjaya;
(औ), du. Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa.

काकुद्र, अस्, आ, अम्, furnished with a palate (?),
a palate (?).

काकोचिक काकोचिक, अस्, m. or काकोची, f. or
काकोचिन्, ई, m. the fish Cyprinus Cachius.

काक्षतव काक्षतव, अम्, n. the fruit of
Kakṣatu.

काक्षसेनि काक्षसेनि, इस्, m. (a patronymic
fr. कक्ष-सेन), an epithet of Abhipratārin.
काक्षि काक्षि, इस्, m., N. of a man.

काक्षी काक्षी, f. a perfume, a fragrant kind
of earth; the plant Cytisus Cajan.

काक्षीव काक्षीव, अस्, m. the plant Hyper-
anthera Moringa; N. of a son of Gautama and of
Auśīnarī, (irregular patronymic fr. कक्षीवत् or
काक्षीवत्.)

काक्षीवक, अस्, m. the plant Hyperanthera Mo-
ringa.

काक्षीवत, अस्, ई, अम्, composed by or relating
to Kakṣīvat; (a patronymic fr. कक्षीवत्), epi-
thet of Śambara.
